newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul Stock Exchange to list two new firms.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul Stock Exchange to list two new firms.

text.p: Turkish airport ground handling firm Celebi Hava Servisi A.S. and investment trust Garanti Yatirim Ortakligi A.S. will be listed on the national market of the Istanbul Stock Exchange on November 18, the exchange said in a statement.
It said the opening price per 1,000 lira nominal-valued share would be 21,000 lira for Celebi and 1,050 lira for Garanti Yatirim Ortakligi.
Celebi, largely owned by Celebi Holding and family, had floated 37.5 billion lira nominal-valued, or 15 percent of its capital, at a 21,000 lira fixed price on November 7-8.
Consortium leader T.Sinai Kalkinma Bankasi said in a statement the public offer was oversubscribed twofold.

It said 18.3 billion lira of the offer was sold to 18,300 domestic individual investors, 15.7 billion lira to 15 international institutional investors, 2.5 billion lira to 22 domestic institutional investors and one billion to company employees.
It added that Fidelity European Trust acquired 2.038 billion lira worth shares, Alliance Capital 2.2 billion and ABN Amro five billion lira in the public offer.
The Turkish ground handling market is divided between Celebi and Havas which was privatised last year.
Celebi which services 112 airlines, posted 718.3 billion lira of net profits and 4.3 trillion lira of net sales provisionally in the first nine months of 1996.
Its net profits stood at 464.3 billion and net sales at 3.6 trillion in the whole of 1995.
Garanti Yatirim Ortakligi has offered to the public 80 percent of its 250 billion lira capital on November 7-8 at a fixed price of 1,050 lira per 1,000 lira nominal valued share.
Consortium leader Garanti Yatirim ve Ticaret Bankasi, also the main shareholder in the investment trust before the flotation, said a total of 1,298 domestic individual investors bought the offer.
